_comment: Tier-2 for fenics helmholtz#2: at high wavenumber an off-the-shelf preconditioner gives up on the Helmholtz operator and the shifted-Laplacian preconditioner is what makes GMRES work. The fixture solves k = 100 on a 32x32 unit square, P1, complex PETSc build, Gaussian source, un-restarted GMRES, rtol 1e-8, 1000 iterations, with three preconditioners: ILU, Jacobi, and a petsc4py python PC that applies the exact inverse of the same form assembled with the complex shift (1 + 0.5i)k^2. Observed on dolfinx 0.10.0 in the fenicsc (complex128) env: ILU returns reason -3 DIVERGED_MAX_IT with a relative residual of 8.685e+00, i.e. the residual is larger than the right-hand side after 1000 iterations; the shifted-Laplacian PC converges in 197 iterations, Jacobi in 509. TWO CORRECTIONS to the claim text are pinned as computed checks. First, the claim's '~10 iterations per convergence' for the shifted Laplacian is false: shifted_laplacian_converged_in_about_ten_iterations=False (197 iterations), and the count scales with k (82 at k = 50 on the same mesh), which is the known O(k) behaviour of a beta = O(1) shift. Second, the claim's 'ILU/Jacobi stagnates at residual ~1e-2' is true only of ILU here; Jacobi does converge on a problem this small. Mutation control: T2_MUTATE=1 puts the shifted-Laplacian PC under test in place of ILU, and the divergence signal disappears. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 with /home/alexander/miniconda3/envs/fenicsc/bin/python (dolfinx 0.10.0, complex128 PETSc); every expect_in_output string was copied from that run.
